implementation_notes: A map from name to a func value is the whole kit, and the standard library shows both halves of the convention: database/sql registers drivers with sql.Register(name, driver) into a mutex-guarded map and dispatches by name in sql.Open, while image.RegisterFormat pairs a name and a decode function that image.Decode later looks up. Drivers register from init() and the host triggers it with a blank import, so registration is invisible at the call site. For your own types declare a Factory func type, keep the map package-private behind a sync.RWMutex, panic on a duplicate key exactly as sql.Register does, and return an error naming the key when Create finds nothing. What replaces the classic structure: the map plus these conventions - a Go interface is the product type, so no factory class exists. Where the set of products is closed, a switch over an enum-like type is simpler and compiler-checked.
pitfalls: init()-time registration is invisible in the source: forget the blank import and the key is simply missing at run time, so registration tests must exercise the same imports as main.
Silently overwriting a duplicate key hides two packages fighting over one name; follow database/sql and panic on duplicates instead.
Map iteration order is randomized and a concurrent write during a read is a data race: sort any 'available names' output and protect the map with the mutex on both paths.
